candidates.summary: Only ProposeHide and ProposeSpotlight get executed through GovDAO. The ProposeUnhide, ProposePause and ProposeUnpause executors never run in any test, yet store_test.gno:875-876 says GovDAO execution is covered by this txtar
candidates.failure_scenario: Change the executor closure of ProposeUnhide (admin.gno, `func() error { return unhide(path) }`) or of ProposePause (`paused = true`) to return nil without doing anything. The txtar stays green, because it only votes on proposals 0 (hide) and 1 (pick). gno test on the realm stays green too, because TestProposals (store_test.gno:878-885) only builds the three requests and never executes them. So a GovDAO unhide or pause vote that passes and changes nothing would ship with every test green.

Then set the Unhide and Pause closures in admin.gno to `func() error { return nil }`, run `go test ./gno.land/pkg/integration -run 'TestTestdata/store_govdao'` and `gno test ./examples/gno.land/r/gnoland/store/v0`, and observe both stay green
candidates.evidence: The txtar's Propose* calls are only ProposeHide (line 68) and ProposeSpotlight (line 80). A repo-wide grep finds ProposeUnhide/ProposePause/ProposeUnpause only at store_test.gno:881,883,884, where they are built and never executed. store_test.gno:875-876: 'Execution by GovDAO is covered by the integration test store_govdao.txtar'.

candidates.summary: The only Register call made from outside the store package is this refused one, made from a filetest main. No test deploys a realm whose init calls store.Register, the path the realm documents as the normal one, and none covers an accepted Register from a real external realm
candidates.failure_scenario: The realm documents Register as called from the app realm's own init at deploy time, with the calling realm's path as proof of control (store.gno:54-68). Every accepted Register in the tests is simulated in-package with testing.SetRealm(testing.NewCodeRealm(path)) (store_test.gno:22-25). This filetest calls Register from main and only for the bad_category refusal, while its comment speaks of 'the caller's init'. So a regression in how cur.Previous().PkgPath() resolves when a realm's init cross-calls Register during addpkg/loadpkg, or in the accepted path from an external realm, ships with every test green. Also, the Render("c/utilities") line adds nothing as a witness: a 'casino' listing could never appear under utilities.
candidates.verify_by: grep -rn 'store\.Register(' --include='*.gno' --include='*.txtar' --include='*.go' . finds only store.gno:60 (a doc comment) and this filetest's line 9. Add a txtar that loadpkg's a $WORK realm with `func init(cur realm) { store.Register(cross(cur), ...) }` and queries api/v1/category/<cat>/1 for its slug
candidates.evidence: grep output: examples/gno.land/r/gnoland/store/v0/store.gno:60 (doc comment) and filetests/register_rejected_filetest.gno:9 only. store_test.gno:23 shows `testing.SetRealm(testing.NewCodeRealm(path))` before every in-package Register.

candidates.summary: For a title of two or more words, initials takes each word's first rune rather than its first letter or digit, so a word that starts with punctuation puts a symbol in the generated icon
candidates.failure_scenario: Title "#1 Wallet": strings.Fields gives ["#1","Wallet"]. DeleteFunc keeps both, since each contains an alphanumeric, and the default branch then decodes '#', so the icon reads "#W". "(Beta) Swap" gives "(S", "@gno Notes" gives "@N" and "$GNOT Faucet" gives "$F". The single-word path strips non-alphanumerics through wordParts, and TestInitials pins that intent with "★ Swap" → "SW". The fix is to decode from p[strings.IndexFunc(p, isAlnum):], which DeleteFunc guarantees is >= 0.
candidates.verify_by: Add `"(Beta) Swap": "BS"` and `"#1 Wallet": "1W"` to TestInitials and run `go test ./gno.land/pkg/gnoweb/feature/store -run TestInitials`. Expect the failures to show "(S" and "#W"
candidates.evidence: cover.go:100-102 `for _, p := range parts[:2] { r, _ := utf8.DecodeRuneInString(p); out = append(out, unicode.ToUpper(r)) }`. cover.go:90 drops only words with no alphanumeric at all. store_test.gno TestInitials has no multi-word case with a punctuation-led word.
